claim:
Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\), where
\[
N(s,t)=\max\{|s|,|t|,|s-t|\}.
\]
Then
\[
C_Z(X)=\frac54.
\]
Moreover, a nonzero pair \((x,y)\) attains \(C_Z(X)\) if and only if, after possibly exchanging \(x\) and \(y\), there exist \(r>0\), signs \(\varepsilon,\delta\in\{-1,1\}\), and a linear isometry \(T\) of \(X\) such that
\[
x=\varepsilon r\,T(0,1),
\qquad
y=\delta r\,T\!\left(-\frac12,-\frac14\right).
\]
Equivalently, in every maximizing pair the larger vector has twice the norm of the smaller one; after normalization the larger vector points to a vertex of the affine-regular hexagonal unit ball and the smaller vector points to the midpoint of the corresponding opposite-adjacent side orbit. Thus the classical counterexample value \(C_Z=5/4\) has a single maximizing orbit modulo the natural dihedral symmetries, independent vector signs, exchange, and common scaling.
integrity: The scalar value is independently reproved. The upper bound exhausts all nine active-functional products; the six distinct-functional products reduce to one exact two-by-two spectral inequality, and equality is traced through every step. Symbolic expansion was used only to verify identities already proved algebraically.
scientific_limitations: The result is restricted to the real affine-regular hexagonal plane. It does not classify Zbăganu maximizers for arbitrary hexagonal norms or higher dimensions. The original 2006 counterexample paper and the full 2010 article were not available through the checked lawful full-text routes.
title: Complete Zbăganu extremizers of the affine-regular hexagonal plane
